assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks at the 10^-18 level are a clean, concrete advance in what can be measured and how accurately. Katori's magic-wavelength lattice concept removed the Doppler and recoil limits for neutral atoms, and Ye's group pushed stability and systematic control to a regime that enables tests of relativity, searches for varying constants, relativistic geodesy and a path to redefining the second. From the laser-spectroscopy tradition I know well, this is a decisive and lasting result.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice idea and first realised it; Ye demonstrated record stability and accuracy and the many-body clock. Two laureates give a defensible configuration. Other groups (e.g. ion-clock and lattice-clock efforts elsewhere) contributed, and the broader metrology field has overlapping credit that a two-name split leaves out.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent labs now reproduce clocks at the 10^-18 level, comparisons across institutes and remote links exist, and the interpretation is very stable. Timely rather than premature; the 2005 prize recognised the comb and earlier spectroscopy, so this is a distinct successor advance.
uncertainties: The redefinition of the second is not yet complete, so the practical culmination is still pending.
Overlap with ion-clock work and the 2012 prize for trapped-ion control may be argued by colleagues as partial precedent.
I have a personal connection to the Hall laboratory tradition from which this field descends; I flag it and do not claim to have verified the detailed credit history independently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum interfaces between light and matter, including cavity QED single-atom links, atomic-ensemble memories and EIT-based storage, underpin quantum repeaters and networks. The concept is original and the experimental realisations are deep. This is close to my own field of quantum memories in solids and gases.
assessment.attribution: Rempe (single-atom cavity-QED network nodes, photon-atom state transfer), Kimble (quantum-network vision, DLCZ-type work with ensembles, cavity QED) and Lukin (EIT-based storage and quantum-network proposals) are plausible, but the field of memories is wide, and rare-earth-crystal and warm-vapour approaches, which I know first-hand, are not represented in this trio. A three-way split is not unique.
assessment.maturity: Memories and elementary links have been shown independently in several platforms, but practical long-distance networks and high-efficiency, long-lived memories are still developing. Recognition is plausible but arguably a few years early for a unified network claim.
uncertainties: The candidate is a compound discovery whose parts (cavity QED, ensemble memories, solid-state memories) may need different recognition.
I have a disclosed professional interest through my own quantum-memory work and European collaborations, which should be weighed when judging my own ranking.
Which individuals are decisive for ensemble storage versus single-atom links is disputed in the literature as far as I know.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposals for trapped-ion quantum gates and for quantum simulation with cold atoms and ions provided the theoretical blueprint for two experimental platforms that later became prize-recognised (2012 for single-quantum-system control) and are now central to quantum technology. The originality and influence are very high.
assessment.attribution: The pair is a natural, compact configuration for the theory; the credited names are exactly the two decisive theorists. Experimental realisation credit is largely already recognised or sits in other candidates (ions, lattice simulators), so this pairing avoids it.
assessment.maturity: Decades of experimental confirmation across ions, atoms and Rydberg systems; the interpretation is stable. The prize would be about theory that experiments have validated rather than a new result. Timely, although the 2012 prize partially covers the experimental side.
uncertainties: Overlap with the optical-lattice simulation candidate (the same two names appear there) could create a conflict if both are recognised.
Whether the committee prefers theory-led recognition when the experimental parent prize was awarded in 2012 is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated matter in optical lattices, including the superfluid to Mott insulator transition, quantum-gas microscopes and fermionic Hubbard studies, turned ultracold-atom control into a general tool for many-body physics. The impact on condensed-matter and quantum-information science is large and lasting.
assessment.attribution: The credited list has five names, so a maximum of three requires a choice. Bloch, Greiner and Esslinger are the experimentalists who defined the observables and the platforms; Cirac and Zoller are the theorists (and are proposed in B034). Hänsch/Greiner/Bloch Mott work, and the Esslinger fermion work, argue for this experimental trio; I acknowledge that the choice leaves out important people.
assessment.maturity: Many independent groups reproduce and extend the results; the field is mature, and microscopy and fermion Hubbard milestones have been reached. Recognition is timely, although the 2001 BEC and 2012 prizes partly neighbour it.
uncertainties: Fair allocation among five credited names is not resolvable inside a three-person limit.
The platform's relationship to the competing Rydberg-array candidate is not settled in my mind.
Overlap with B034 means only one of these two candidates is likely to be recognised.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom interferometry turns matter waves into precision sensors for gravity, rotation and tests of the equivalence principle and the fine-structure constant. The measurement-driven nature of the field matches the idea that technical progress is limited by what can be measured and how accurately, a point I have made in a sensing context only. The conceptual originality (atom optics, light-pulse interferometers) is strong.
assessment.attribution: Bordé (early theoretical and spectroscopic interferometer ideas), Pritchard (first atom interferometers and atomic-beam optics) and Kasevich (light-pulse interferometers and precision gravimetry/gyroscopes) form a plausible trio. Chu, Chu-group credit and others that share the heritage are not on the list as given; some credit for the field was recognised by the 1997 prize on cooling and the 2001 BEC prize.
assessment.maturity: Many independent groups, commercial gravimeters and large baseline experiments exist, but the large-scale fundamental-physics payoffs (gravitational-wave detection, dark-matter searches) are still prospective. Mature as a technique, partly premature as a discovery claim.
uncertainties: Credit among atom-interferometry pioneers is partly disputed or spread across many labs.
Whether the major fundamental-physics results have appeared yet or are still to come is unsettled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED brought the strong-coupling cavity-QED paradigm to superconducting circuits and is the architecture of most superconducting quantum processors. The concept is original, clear and broadly influential. I regard it as connected to my field because the physics is light-matter coupling with artificial atoms.
assessment.attribution: Blais and Girvin (with Wallraff and others) provided the theory and Schoelkopf's group the experiment; Wallraff is not in the credited names, so the allocation within the credited trio is imperfect. The macroscopic quantum tunnelling prize of 2025 already recognised a superconducting-circuit foundation, which may reduce appetite for another circuit prize soon.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed across many groups and used in commercial devices. Timely in content, but the committee may judge the cluster of superconducting-circuit recognition as recently addressed.
uncertainties: Omitted people (notably Wallraff) cannot be added; the allocation within the supplied names is uncertain.
The relation to the very recent circuit-based prize is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Squeezed light for interferometry is a conceptually elegant use of quantum optics, now implemented in gravitational-wave detectors to beat the standard quantum limit. It is an excellent example of quantum measurement theory becoming practice.
assessment.attribution: Caves proposed the idea; Kimble led the first squeezed-state experiments and Schnabel the GEO600 and subsequent implementations; Mavalvala led later LIGO-scale work and could be preferable to Schnabel or Kimble. The assignment is contested, and no triple is clearly right.
assessment.maturity: Operating in detectors for several years, independently confirmed by LIGO, Virgo and GEO. The gravitational-wave prize of 2017 has already recognised the detector discovery, so this is a distinct but subordinate advance.
uncertainties: Credit allocation between theory, early lab demonstrations and detector integration is unresolved.
The committee may consider it a technological refinement of an already recognised discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Trapping, cooling and precision spectroscopy of antihydrogen and antiprotons (and electron g-factor work) test CPT and matter-antimatter symmetry. It is technically demanding atomic physics with deep fundamental motivation.
assessment.attribution: Gabrielse (precise electron and positron/antiproton measurements, antihydrogen trapping at ATRAP) and Hangst (ALPHA antihydrogen trapping and spectroscopy) are sensible, but the antihydrogen result was achieved by collaborations and also by ATHENA/ASACUSA/AEgIS groups that are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Results are reproduced in several experiments, but precision comparisons are still improving, and no violation has been seen. Whether the prize would be about a discovery or about a continuing method is unclear, which suggests it is somewhat premature.
uncertainties: Collaboration-based credit is hard to restrict to two people.
No symmetry violation has been found, so the scientific payoff is a null-result precision test, which committee members may weigh differently.
